text.p: Former British Open champion Ian Baker-Finch had a miserable return to golf on Thursday when he carded a five-over-par 77 in the first round of the Victorian Open.

Baker-Finch, who took six months away from tournament golf after a succession of poor results in recent years, was a massive 13 shots behind leader and defending champion Stephen Leaney at the end of the first round.

Leaney fired a new course record of eight-under-par 64 to lead the tournament by two strokes from Paul Devenport of New Zealand. Australians Rob Whitlock and Shane Tait were a further shot back on 67 in joint third.
Baker-Finch, winner of the 1991 British Open, has made the halfway cut in only one tournament in over two years but started well with a par on his first hole.

The affable Australian was two-over after his first nine holes and drew level with the card after an eagle two on the short par-four first, his 10th hole. But he then dropped five shots on his next eight holes to fall well behind the leaders.
"I'm going to give myself six out of 10," Baker-Finch later told reporters.
"I really didn't trust myself for the last four or five holes. The wind got really strong and I played some poor tee shots."
Leaney's round bettered by two shots the previous course record held by Australians Robert Allenby, Peter O'Malley and Peter Fowler since 1995.
Starting his round from the 10th tee, Leaney picked up four shots on his first nine holes and then, like Baker-Finch, made an eagle two at the first hole on his inward nine.
"I didn't know what the course record was and I wasn't thinking about it," Leaney said.
